tolerance.full: tolerance to sedative effects develops with continued use

addictionPotential: low addiction potential; not typically abused
toxicities: Weight gain, increased risk of type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, extrapyramidal symptoms (less than other antipsychotics)
summary: Olanzapine is a widely used atypical antipsychotic of the thienobenzodiazepine class. It produces sedation and neuroleptic effects. It can be used for trip termination, especially for stimulant-related situations, as it blocks dopamine action.
effectsSummary: Sedation, increased appetite, muscle relaxation, motor control loss, dizziness, anxiety suppression, emotional blunting, cognitive suppression, body heaviness.
dosageRemark: Bioavailability is 60-65% orally. Effects vary significantly between individuals. Therapeutic doses start at 2.5-5mg for antipsychotic effects.
generalRisks: Weight gain, drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, extrapyramidal symptoms. More likely to cause weight gain and diabetes than other antipsychotics.
longtermRisks: Significant weight gain, increased risk of type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia (lower risk than typical antipsychotics). May cause cognitive dulling.
saferUse: Only use as prescribed by a doctor
Monitor weight and blood sugar regularly
Avoid alcohol and other CNS depressants
Do not use for trip termination without medical supervision
